md_name: iPSC genetic stability under culture conditions
md_description: This workflow tracks donor-derived iPSC lines through controlled culture condition variants and genomic stability assays. It captures how media supplements, oxygen tension, and passaging technique influence genomic integrity across passages using SNP arrays and whole-genome sequencing. The resulting raw signals are processed into aberration summaries and phenotypic summaries, then integrated into a metadata-rich dataset for identifying culture conditions that best preserve genetic stability.

ipsc_lines.reasoning: For the Entity node ipsc_lines, I included only intrinsic identity and origin fields: donor linkage, donor demographics, source/original cell type, reprogramming origin context, and baseline line identity/quality attributes. I excluded anything about culture conditions, passages, SNP/WGS assays, raw signal files, or derived aberration/phenotype outputs because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided fields already implied by the DAG’s integrated metadata target that would be repeated elsewhere, and kept identifiers limited to the root entity territory rather than downstream measurement or analysis identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each induced pluripotent stem cell line in the study; use a stable string such as IPSC_001 or donorA_line2. Assigned once at the entity level and used to link all downstream culture, assay, and analysis records.

Unique donor identifier for the individual from whom the iPSC line was derived; format example DONOR_01. This is an intrinsic provenance field for the starting biological material and should not be repeated as a measurement or process output.

Biological sex of the donor recorded at source material collection, before reprogramming; use the study's donor annotation standard. Typical values are male or female, with unknown allowed if not available.

Donor age in years at the time the original somatic cells were collected for reprogramming; integer or decimal years may be used if the source record is not whole-number. Typical range in this study is expected to be adult donors, for example 18 to 90 years.

Self-reported or source-record ethnicity/race category for the donor, as captured in the original donor metadata. Use the study's controlled vocabulary; common values may include categories such as asian, black, white, hispanic_or_latino, mixed, other, or unknown.

Original somatic cell type used to derive the iPSC line, recorded before reprogramming; examples include fibroblast, peripheral_blood_mononuclear_cell, or keratinocyte. This describes the source cell identity, not any culture manipulation.

Anatomical tissue or specimen source of the starting somatic cells used to generate the iPSC line; for example skin, blood, or urine. This is an origin attribute of the line rather than a culture or assay parameter.

Method used to generate the iPSC line from the donor's starting cells, captured as a provenance attribute of the line itself; examples include integrating viral vectors, non-integrating episomal methods, Sendai virus, or mRNA-based reprogramming.

Baseline chromosomal status of the iPSC line as recorded prior to the culture-condition experiment, if available; examples include normal or abnormal. This is an intrinsic starting-line quality attribute, not the result of SNP-array or WGS processing in the study workflow.

Whether the starting iPSC line was confirmed to be pluripotent before entering the culture-condition study, based on source records or prior qualification. This is a yes/no/unknown entity attribute and not a downstream assay readout.

culture_condition_application.reasoning: For the Process node culture_condition_application, I included only the operational parameters of how the iPSC lines were expanded under controlled culture variants: media composition/supplements, oxygen tension, passaging technique, timing/frequency, seeding density, confluency target, and a process-level outcome/quality indicator for the culture step. I excluded donor or line identity because that belongs to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded cultured population attributes, passage state after expansion, raw assay files, or genomic/phenotypic results because those belong to downstream Entity, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided duplicating any IDs or demographic fields from the prior node.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the culture protocol variant applied to an iPSC line during this process step; use a stable string such as CP_001 or lowO2_mediaA_passageB. This identifies the exact combination of culture settings used in this process.

Controlled set of media supplements used during expansion in this process step; record the study vocabulary or formula label rather than free text when possible. Examples may include bfgf_insulin, xeno_free, or feeder_free supplement sets.

Target oxygen concentration used during culture expansion, measured and set at the incubator or chamber during this process step; typical values in this study may range from 2 to 21 percent depending on atmospheric or low-oxygen conditions.
Technique used to passage the iPSC cultures during the application step; choose the controlled vocabulary term that matches the actual split method used for the line at this step.

Total duration of the expansion period under this protocol variant, measured from start to end of the applied culture condition window; report in hours with typical study ranges from a few tens to several hundred hours.

Passage number reached or used at the end of this culture-condition application step; integer count recorded after expansion under the specified conditions. Typical values are sequential passage integers such as 1 to 30+ depending on the line.

Cell seeding density used at the start of the culture step, measured as cells per square centimeter. Record the planned or executed density applied to the culture vessel at the time this process began; typical values are study-specific and often in the low thousands to tens of thousands.

Target confluency percentage used to decide when the culture step should proceed or be passaged; measured visually or by imaging at the point of process control. Typical values are often 70 to 90 percent depending on the protocol.

Identifier for a replicate culture instance executed under the same or similar protocol settings; use a stable string such as REP_01. This distinguishes parallel culture runs within the same line and protocol combination.

Overall quality outcome for this culture-condition application step, summarizing whether the culture was carried out successfully according to protocol. Use a controlled vocabulary such as pass, warning, or fail based on adherence to the intended conditions and culture health.

cultured_ipsc_lines.reasoning: For the Entity node cultured_ipsc_lines, I included only the intrinsic state of the resulting cultured populations after the process step: linkage back to the source iPSC line and applied protocol, current passage state, culture state/stability descriptors, morphology/growth status, and whether the population remained available for downstream capture and analysis. I excluded culture settings themselves because those belong to the upstream process, and I excluded SNP/WGS, phenotype observations, raw files, and derived aberration summaries because those belong to downstream capture/signal/derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating donor demographics and original cell type from ipsc_lines, and I did not use any field already generated for the application process that would be semantically equivalent.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the cultured iPSC population instance resulting from the application of a specific culture protocol; use a stable string such as CULT_001 or lineA_pass5_lowO2. This is the entity-level identifier for the maintained population, not the original line ID.
Identifier of the upstream donor iPSC line from which this cultured population was derived; example format IPSC_001. This field links the cultured population back to the originating entity.

Identifier of the culture protocol variant under which this population was maintained; example format CP_001. This links the population to the applied culture-condition process without restating the protocol details.

Passage number of the cultured iPSC population at the time it is considered for downstream assays or storage; integer count recorded after maintenance under the study condition. Typical values are sequential passages such as 1 to 30+.

General state of the cultured population at the defined passage, summarizing whether the cells are healthy and usable for downstream analysis. Use controlled terms that describe the entity state rather than a procedure or measurement result.

Observed gross morphology of the cultured iPSC population at the time this entity record is made, such as compact_colonies or differentiated_outgrowth. This is an entity-level descriptive attribute rather than a separate phenotype assay summary.

Qualitative growth behavior of the cultured population at the recorded passage, reflecting whether the culture expanded normally under the applied conditions. Use a study-defined categorical assessment rather than a numeric growth curve.

Approximate viable cell fraction for the cultured population at the time of passage or assay readiness, measured as percent viable cells. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and are recorded for the entity state after culture maintenance.
Whether this cultured population was cryopreserved after maintenance under the study condition and passage state. Use true if aliquots were banked, false if not, or unknown if not recorded.

snp_array_capture.reasoning: For the Capture node snp_array_capture, I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields: instrument identity, manufacturer, model, serial number, array platform/kit, assay date, sample input state at the time of capture, and the key run settings needed to reproduce the capture. I excluded donor, line, and culture attributes because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file-format, file-size, and probe-intensity outputs because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided duplication of process-level culture settings and downstream SNP aberration summaries. The fields focus on the actively configured capture environment and the minimal session metadata needed to interpret the raw SNP array signal.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP array capture session; use a stable string such as CAP_SNP_001. This identifier marks the specific measurement session for a cultured iPSC sample at a selected passage.
Manufacturer of the microarray instrument used for SNP array capture; for example Illumina. Record the hardware vendor for the active capture platform.

Model name or number of the microarray instrument used for SNP array capture; example format iScan or equivalent platform-specific model. Record the exact hardware model used during the measurement session.
Serial number of the microarray instrument used for this SNP array capture session; example format SN123456. This uniquely identifies the active hardware instance used to generate the raw signal.
Name of the SNP array kit or chip used in the capture session; for example a specific genome-wide SNP array product or beadchip type. Record the assay kit actually used for the measurement.
Date on which the SNP array measurement was performed for the cultured iPSC sample at the selected passage; record in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD.

Amount of DNA input loaded into the SNP array capture, measured in nanograms at the time of assay setup. Typical study values may range from tens to hundreds of nanograms depending on kit requirements.

Passage number of the cultured iPSC population at the time the SNP array capture was performed; integer count recorded from the source sample. Typical values follow the study passage series such as 1 to 30+.

Key instrument scan settings used during SNP array capture, such as resolution or gain parameters, recorded as the active configuration for the measurement session. Use a concise controlled string or lab-standard settings label.

Overall quality indicator for the SNP array capture session, summarizing whether the run met instrument and assay acceptance criteria. Use controlled values indicating successful capture or problems with the session.

snp_raw_signal.reasoning: For the Signal node snp_raw_signal, I included only raw data artefact properties: file identity, file format, file size, storage location, number of arrays/channels or data dimensions, and technical quality/completeness metrics. I excluded instrument model and scan settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded genotype interpretation, copy-number calls, and aberration summaries because those belong to the downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any sample or passage identifiers that were already assigned earlier in the workflow, focusing instead on the file-level characteristics needed to find, validate, and reuse the raw SNP array data.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw SNP array file produced by the capture session; use a stable string such as SNPRAW_001 or sampleA_pass5_idat. This identifies the file-level artefact rather than the biological sample.

Digital file format of the raw SNP array output; record the actual on-disk format used for storage, such as idat, txt, or other vendor-specific raw formats. This is a technical property of the raw artefact.
File size of the raw SNP array output in bytes, measured from the stored artefact. Typical values depend on array density and may range from millions to billions of bytes.
Storage location or URI for the raw SNP array file; example format s3://bucket/path/file.idat or a local file path. This enables retrieval of the raw data artefact.

Raw signal matrix dimensions for the SNP array output, recorded as the number of probes by the number of channels or equivalent vendor-specific dimensions. This describes the technical shape of the raw file, not a biological result.

Total number of probes represented in the raw SNP array file, as reported by the array platform or file header. Typical values are study- and array-specific and often in the hundreds of thousands to millions.

Percent of expected raw probe signal entries successfully present in the file at the time of QA; used as a technical completeness metric for the raw artefact. Typical values are near 100 percent for acceptable runs.

Technical quality assessment for the raw SNP array artefact itself, indicating whether the file is readable and complete enough for downstream processing. Use controlled values for acceptable, degraded, or unusable raw data.

wgs_capture.reasoning: I corrected the WGS capture schema by removing the two colliding field names that were already generated earlier in the DAG: capture_date and capture_quality_flag. To preserve the capture-node semantics without duplicating prior metadata, I replaced them with WGS-specific equivalents that remain in the measurement-session territory and do not overlap with upstream or downstream nodes. The rest of the fields continue to describe instrument identity and actively controlled sequencing settings only.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the whole-genome sequencing capture session; use a stable string such as WGS_CAP_001. This marks the specific sequencing run performed on a cultured iPSC sample at a selected passage.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for whole-genome sequencing capture; for example Illumina. Record the hardware vendor of the active sequencer.
Model name or number of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session; example format NovaSeq 6000 or equivalent. Record the exact sequencer model operating during the run.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for this whole-genome sequencing session; example format SN987654. This uniquely identifies the instrument instance that produced the raw reads.

Sequencing chemistry or platform configuration used in the WGS run; record the active chemistry version or kit name applied during capture. This is a hardware/assay configuration attribute of the session.

Library preparation mode used immediately before sequencing capture; examples include PCR_free, PCR_plus, or standard_workflow depending on the protocol used. This describes the configured sequencing session rather than downstream data.

Sequencing read length in base pairs configured for the WGS run, measured at the instrument setup stage; typical values may include 100, 150, or longer paired-end reads. Record the nominal read length used for capture.
Intended average sequencing depth in fold coverage for the WGS capture session; for example 30x or 60x. This is the planned configuration used to assess genome-wide stability.

Date on which the whole-genome sequencing run was performed for the cultured iPSC sample; record in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. This field is WGS-specific and replaces the previously used generic capture date field to avoid cross-step collision.

Overall quality indicator for the whole-genome sequencing run, summarizing whether the session met sequencing acceptance criteria. Use controlled values indicating successful run, warnings, or failure; this WGS-specific field replaces the previously used generic capture quality flag to avoid cross-step collision.

wgs_raw_signal.reasoning: For the Signal node wgs_raw_signal, I retained only raw read artefact properties that do not collide with fields already generated earlier in the DAG: file identity, read layout, read count, total bases, and completeness. I removed file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_uri, and raw_signal_quality_flag because they were reported as collisions across DAG steps and therefore must not be repeated. I also continued to exclude any capture-session settings, alignment, variant interpretation, or biological sample attributes, since those belong to upstream or downstream nodes rather than the raw signal artefact itself.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw whole-genome sequencing file or file set produced by the capture session; use a stable string such as WGSRAW_001 or sampleA_R1.fastq.gz. This identifies the file-level artefact rather than the biological sample.

Layout of the raw sequencing reads in the file set, describing how the reads are organized for the WGS output; examples include paired_end or single_end. This is a technical file property, not an instrument configuration.
Total number of reads contained in the raw sequencing file set, as reported by file statistics or header summaries. Typical values are large integers reflecting genome-scale sequencing depth.
Total number of sequenced bases represented in the raw signal, measured in gigabases across the file set. This is a technical size metric useful for assessing raw data completeness.

Percent of expected raw read data successfully present in the stored file set at the time of QA; used as a technical completeness metric for the raw artefact. Typical values are near 100 percent for acceptable runs.

snp_processing.reasoning: For the Process node snp_processing, I included only computational workflow properties: software/pipeline identity, version, repository, core algorithm or normalization method, key processing parameters, and process-level output quality/acceptance metrics. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the Signal node, and I excluded the resulting aberration summary itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating fields already used elsewhere in the DAG, especially generic file and capture fields, and kept the schema focused on how the SNP array intensities were transformed into analysis-ready summaries.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP array processing run; use a stable string such as SNPPROC_001. This identifies the computational execution that converts raw SNP intensities into analysis outputs.

Name of the software or pipeline used to process the SNP array data; for example GenomeStudio, PennCNV, or a lab-specific pipeline. This field belongs on the processing node because it identifies the analysis tool that performed the transformation.
Version of the SNP processing software or pipeline used for this run; example format 2.1.0 or v3.4. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of the computed results.

Source repository or distribution reference for the SNP processing software, such as a Git URL, package registry, or internal code base identifier. This documents the implementation used in the processing step.

Normalization or preprocessing method applied to SNP intensities before genotype or copy-number inference; examples include quantile_normalization or vendor_default_normalization. Record the method used in this processing run.

Algorithm used to infer copy-number variation from the processed SNP intensities; for example circular binary segmentation, hidden Markov model, or a study-specific caller. This is a processing parameter, not the final derived call.
Identifier of the raw SNP array signal file or file set fed into this processing run; example format SNPRAW_001. This links the process back to the upstream signal artefact.

Threshold or confidence criterion used when assigning genotype calls from SNP intensities during processing; record the value or setting applied in this workflow. Typical thresholds are study- and platform-specific.
Elapsed runtime of the SNP processing job in minutes, measured from job start to completion. This is a process execution metric useful for tracking computational performance.

Overall quality assessment for the SNP processing run, indicating whether the computation completed successfully and produced usable outputs. Use controlled values describing successful, warning, or failed processing.

snp_aberration_table.reasoning: For the Derivative node snp_aberration_table, I included only computed-result fields: derivative table identity, source signal/process linkage, the genomic aberration categories summarized, counts and genome burden metrics, affected chromosomes/regions, and a derivative-level confidence or quality indicator. I excluded software and algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the Signal node. I also avoided using capture-date or generic file fields that have already collided elsewhere in the DAG. The schema is focused on what the computed aberration table contains and how strong the inferred genomic instability signal is.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived SNP aberration table; use a stable string such as SNPAB_001. This identifies the computed result object rather than the raw data or processing job.
Identifier of the raw SNP array signal used to generate this aberration table; example format SNPRAW_001. This links the derivative back to the upstream input artefact.
Identifier of the SNP processing run that produced the aberration table; example format SNPPROC_001. This links the derivative to the computational transformation that generated it.

Type of genomic aberration summarized in the table, such as copy_number_gain, copy_number_loss, loh, or aneuploidy. If multiple aberration classes are represented, use the study's controlled vocabulary or one row per type depending on table structure.

Count of aberrant events detected in the SNP-derived summary for the sample or table row, such as number of copy-number changes or structural abnormalities. This is a derived integer count produced by the analysis.

Estimated percentage of the genome affected by the detected aberrations, measured as percent of genomic bases or segments involved. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate the burden of instability.

Chromosomes implicated by the aberration calls in this derived summary, recorded as a comma-separated string or compact code list such as 1,7,12,X. This is a result field describing which chromosomes were affected.

Genomic coordinate summary for the aberrant regions reported in the table, using a study-standard representation such as chr:start-end or region identifiers. This field captures the location of the derived events rather than raw probe positions.

Confidence or support score for the derived aberration summary, as produced by the SNP analysis workflow; higher values indicate stronger support for the call set. Record the scale used by the pipeline if applicable.

Overall quality assessment of the derived aberration table, reflecting whether the computed calls are complete and suitable for downstream integration. Use controlled values indicating acceptable, degraded, or failed derivative quality.

wgs_processing.reasoning: For the WGS processing node, I kept only process-specific computation fields that do not collide with earlier DAG steps: pipeline identity, reference/alignment choices, variant and structural caller settings, filtering thresholds, and a processing-specific output checksum/quality metric. I removed software_name, software_version, software_repository, process_runtime_minutes, and processing_quality_flag because those fields had already been generated elsewhere in the DAG and must not be repeated. I also excluded raw-read properties and derived variant summaries because those belong to the Signal and Derivative nodes, respectively.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the whole-genome sequencing processing run; use a stable string such as WGSPROC_001. This identifies the computational execution that converts raw reads into aligned and variant summaries.

Name or label of the WGS analysis pipeline used for this run, excluding generic software metadata already represented elsewhere; example labels include germline_variant_pipeline or genome_stability_workflow. This identifies the computation at a workflow level.

Reference genome build used for read alignment and downstream variant calling during WGS processing; for example GRCh37 or GRCh38. This is a core processing reference choice and not a property of the raw signal.
Method or aligner used to map raw sequencing reads to the reference genome; examples include bwa_mem, bowtie2, or minimap2. Record the algorithm used in the processing step.

Primary variant calling algorithm used to identify small variants from aligned reads; examples include GATK, FreeBayes, or DeepVariant. This field belongs to the processing node because it is part of the computational transformation.

Algorithm used to infer structural variants or larger genomic rearrangements from aligned reads; examples include Manta, Delly, or a study-specific structural caller. Record the method used in this processing run.
Key numerical threshold used to filter aligned reads or variant candidates during WGS processing, such as minimum base quality or variant support. Record the value and scale used by the pipeline.
Whether duplicate reads were marked or removed during WGS processing prior to variant calling. Use true if duplicate handling was applied, false if it was skipped, or unknown if not recorded.

Percentage of raw reads that successfully aligned to the reference genome during processing, computed as a summary metric of mapping performance. Typical values are between 0 and 100 percent and reflect the quality of the processing output.

Whether the WGS processing output passed the study's internal QC criteria after alignment and calling, such as coverage, mapping, and filter checks. Use true, false, or unknown as the process-specific acceptance indicator.

wgs_genomic_calls.reasoning: For the Derivative node wgs_genomic_calls, I kept only result-specific fields that do not collide with prior DAG steps: a unique call-set identifier, compact summaries of small variants and structural aberrations, counts of those events, and a confidence score. I excluded source linkage fields because they have already been used elsewhere in the DAG and would collide, and I excluded generic burden/quality fields that have also been generated previously. I also excluded any software, capture, or raw-file properties because those belong to upstream Process, Capture, and Signal nodes. The remaining fields describe the computed WGS instability result itself.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived whole-genome sequencing call set; use a stable string such as WGSVAR_001. This identifies the computed result object rather than the raw reads or processing job.

Compact summary of small variants detected in the derived WGS result, such as single-nucleotide variants and small insertions/deletions. Record as a study-standard categorical or compact text summary rather than raw variant records.
Compact summary of structural aberrations inferred from WGS, such as deletions, duplications, inversions, or translocations. This is the computed structural result, not the caller configuration.
Total count of small variants represented in the derived WGS call set for the sample or table row. This is a computed integer count from the analysis output.
Total count of structural aberrations represented in the derived WGS result for the sample or table row. This is a computed integer count from the analysis output.

Confidence or support score for the derived small-variant call set, as produced by the WGS analysis workflow; higher values indicate stronger support for the variant calls. Record the scale used by the pipeline if applicable.

Confidence or support score for the derived structural-aberration call set, as produced by the WGS analysis workflow; higher values indicate stronger support for the structural calls. Record the scale used by the pipeline if applicable.

Overall status of the derived WGS call set, reflecting whether the output is complete and suitable for downstream integration. Use controlled values indicating the quality state of the final computed result.

phenotype_assessment.reasoning: For the Process node phenotype_assessment, I included only observation-workflow fields: assessment method, observer, scoring rubric, observation timepoint, assessed morphology/growth categories, and a process-level quality/completeness indicator. I excluded donor and line identity because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded the summarized phenotype table because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any already-generated generic process fields such as software or runtime, since this is a researcher-observation step rather than a computational pipeline. The fields focus on how phenotypic observations were made and standardized before summarization.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the phenotype assessment run; use a stable string such as PHENO_001. This identifies the observation session used to summarize morphological or growth-related changes in cultured iPSC lines.

Method used to assess phenotypic changes during this process step; examples include direct microscopy, time-lapse imaging, or manual visual review. Record the observation approach used to generate the phenotype summary.
Role of the person or team performing the phenotype assessment, such as researcher, technician, or automated review system. This identifies who or what performed the observation step.

Study rubric or scoring framework used to classify observed morphology or growth-related changes, such as normal/abnormal or a multi-level severity scale. Record the rubric used to standardize the assessment.

Time in hours after culture initiation or after the relevant passage at which the phenotypic observation was made. Typical values are study-specific and may range from immediate post-passaging to several days later.

Observed growth-related category assigned during the phenotype assessment, such as normal_growth, slow_growth, or arrested_growth. This is the process-level categorization before derivative summarization.

Observed morphology category assigned during the phenotype assessment, such as compact_colonies, differentiated_outgrowth, or mixed_morphology. This is the process-level categorization before derivative summarization.

Percent of planned phenotype observations completed for the assessed culture set at this process step. This is a process-quality metric used to judge whether the observation session is sufficiently complete for summarization.

Overall quality assessment for the phenotype observation session, indicating whether the assessment was performed consistently and can support downstream summarization. Use controlled values describing pass, warning, fail, or unknown.

phenotype_changes.reasoning: For the Derivative node phenotype_changes, I kept only summary-level phenotype result fields and renamed the upstream link and quality fields to avoid DAG-wide collisions. I included a unique derivative identifier, the linked assessment-process identifier under a new name, the phenotype summary and categorical interpretation, severity, passage association, response label, and observation consistency. I excluded any process-method details, raw image/file properties, and unrelated genomic fields because they belong to other node types. The schema is focused on the final interpreted phenotype record for downstream integration.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived phenotype change summary; use a stable string such as PHENO_SUM_001. This identifies the computed or consolidated phenotype record rather than the observation session itself.
Identifier of the phenotype assessment process that generated this summary; example format PHENO_001. This links the derivative back to the upstream observation workflow.

Concise textual or coded summary of the observed phenotypic changes associated with the culture condition and passage, such as normal morphology, slowed growth, or differentiated outgrowth. This is the main interpreted phenotype result.
Primary category assigned to the observed phenotype change in the derived summary; use a controlled vocabulary that captures the main interpreted outcome of the assessment.

Numeric severity score assigned to the derived phenotype change summary, reflecting the extent of deviation from expected iPSC morphology or growth. Record on the study's scoring scale, typically low to high or 0 to 1/5.

Passage number at which the phenotype change was observed or summarized in the derived record; integer count linking the phenotype outcome to the culture stage. Typical values are sequential passages such as 1 to 30+.

Derived label describing the response of the cultured iPSC line to the applied culture condition, such as stable, sensitive, or deteriorating. This summarizes the phenotype in the context of the experimental culture condition.

Percent consistency across repeated phenotype observations or reviewers, if the derived record aggregates more than one assessment. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate confidence in the summarized phenotype.

Overall quality assessment of the derived phenotype summary, reflecting whether the consolidated record is complete and suitable for downstream integration. Use controlled values indicating acceptable, degraded, or failed derivative quality.

metadata_integration.reasoning: For the Process node metadata_integration, I included only integration-workflow fields: integration run identity, source table linkage, join keys, integration method, record match/completeness metrics, conflict resolution strategy, and an integration quality flag. I excluded donor demographics, culture protocol details, and genomic or phenotype result content because those belong to upstream Entity, Process, and Derivative nodes that are being combined here rather than created here. I also avoided duplicate generic software fields because this is a data-wrangling step whose key metadata are about how disparate records were merged into the final dataset.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the metadata integration run; use a stable string such as METAINT_001. This identifies the computational execution that combines multiple upstream tables into one dataset.

Identifiers of the upstream tables or data objects used as inputs to the integration step, such as SNP aberration tables, WGS call sets, phenotype summaries, and donor or culture metadata tables. Provide a controlled list or delimited string of source identifiers.
Field names used to join the upstream records during integration, such as ipsc_line_id, culture_protocol_id, or passage_number. This describes the linkage strategy used to build the unified dataset.

Method used to merge the upstream tables into a unified metadata dataset; examples include relational_join, key_based_merge, or manual_curated_merge. Record the actual integration approach used in this step.

Strategy used when upstream records disagreed on a field value during integration; examples include prioritize_latest, prioritize_source_of_truth, majority_vote, or manual_review. This is an operational property of the merge step.
Percent of intended upstream records successfully matched and integrated into the unified dataset during this run. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and quantify integration completeness.

Percent of expected fields missing after integration across the assembled dataset, measured as a completeness indicator for the merge output. Typical values range from 0 to 100, with lower values indicating better completeness.
Number of duplicate records or conflicting entries that were detected and resolved during integration. This is a process metric describing the merge effort and data hygiene outcome.
Date on which the metadata integration was executed or finalized; record in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. This marks when the unified dataset was assembled.

Overall quality status for the integration step, indicating whether the combined dataset met expected completeness and consistency criteria. Use controlled values for successful, warning, failed, or unknown integration runs.

integrated_metadata_table.reasoning: For the final Derivative node integrated_metadata_table, I included only table-level output properties that describe the assembled dataset itself: table identifier, row/column dimensions, file/storage format if applicable, the linkage scope of included source domains, completeness/consistency metrics, and a final table quality indicator. I excluded donor demographics, origin cell type, culture protocol details, genomic aberrations, and phenotype content because those are the integrated scientific fields themselves and were already handled in upstream Entity/Process/Derivative nodes or in the final joined records rather than as table-level metadata. I also avoided any fields that collide with previously generated generic file or quality identifiers, and focused on the metadata a downstream user needs to locate, size, and trust the final dataset.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final joined metadata table; use a stable string such as META_TABLE_001. This identifies the derivative dataset object rather than an individual row.
Storage location or URI for the integrated metadata table; example format s3://bucket/path/integrated_metadata.csv or a local file path. This enables retrieval of the final dataset artefact.
File or table format used for the final integrated dataset; examples include csv, tsv, parquet, or database_table. Record the actual delivery format of the derivative table.

Number of rows in the integrated metadata table, typically one row per line-condition-passage-assay combination or study-defined record unit. This is a table-level size metric for the final derivative dataset.
Number of columns in the integrated metadata table after joining all upstream domains. This describes the dimensionality of the final dataset.

List or compact label describing which source domains are represented in the final table, such as donor, culture_protocol, snp_aberration, wgs_calls, and phenotype. This summarizes the integration scope of the derivative dataset.
Percent of intended joined records or fields successfully populated in the final integrated table. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate how complete the assembled dataset is.

Quality score summarizing agreement across joined domains after integration, such as consistency between donor, culture, genomic, and phenotype records. Record the study's score scale if defined; otherwise use a normalized numeric score.
Version label for the integrated metadata table release, such as v1.0 or 2026-08-18_release. This supports downstream provenance and dataset tracking.
